{{Main|Equipment}}
'''Steel equipment''' is iron equipment upgraded with [[Steel Alloy|steel alloy]]. It is very durable, its weapons add knockback, and its armor has knockback resistance and Blast Protection.

== Obtaining ==
Steel alloy is blasted from [[Carbon-Rich Iron|carbon-rich iron]] (four iron ingots and a block of coal make four). Each piece of iron equipment is then upgraded at a [[Smithing Table|smithing table]] with no template; the [[Steel Claymore|steel claymore]] and [[Steel Dolabra|dolabra]] and [[Steel Mattock|mattock]] also need a [[Smithing Upgrade Template|smithing upgrade template]]. Steel is repaired with plain iron ingots.

In the video the developer describes steel as "processed iron that can make iron doubly efficient. It's very durable, knockback and blast resistant, and its tools have a knockback intrinsic."<ref>{{Cite video|quote=Steel, processed iron that can make iron doubly efficient. It's very durable, knockback and blast resistant, and its tools have a knockback intrinsic.}}</ref>

== Notes ==
* The 1.10 notes warn against wearing steel in the [[Abbey]]: "Blast resistance makes the dungeon boring."
* Steel pickaxes and dolabras have no obsidian restriction and mine obsidian with drops.
* In 1.12.2 steel armor is invisible when worn: its equipment asset is <code>minecraft:steel</code>, while the resource pack defines the texture as <code>matcha:steel</code>.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/smithing/steel_chestplate.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/matcha/equipment/steel.json}}</ref>
* In 1.12.2 the steel pickaxe and steel shovel show the game's real attribute lines in their tooltips next to the hand-written ones; the other steel tools hide them.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/smithing/steel_pickaxe.json}}</ref>
